text: Soon after lunch the band, dressed in green coats, took its place in a corner of the tennis court, and Kitty Maitland declared that they looked just like frogs. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura wanted to tell Laurie about the accident, but when he looked at her and said that her hat was absolutely topping, she decided not to tell him after all. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon the guests came streaming in, and Laura moved happily among them, offering ices and smiling, until the perfect afternoon slowly ripened, slowly faded, and slowly closed its petals. <break time="0.8s" /> When the last guest had gone, Mister Sheridan mentioned the ghastly accident, and Missus Sheridan, a little annoyed, said that Laura had wanted them to put off the party. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she had one of her brilliant ideas, and she told Laura to take the leftover sandwiches, cakes, and puffs down to the poor family in a big basket. <break time="0.8s" /> Her mother wanted to add some arum lilies, believing that people of that class were very impressed by them, but Jose warned that the stems would ruin Lauras lace frock. <break time="0.8s" /> As Laura was leaving, her mother called after her, Do not on any account, but then she stopped and only told her to run along. <break time="0.8s" /> It was growing dusky as Laura walked down the hill into the smoky, dark lane, where women in shawls and men in tweed caps hurried past her. <break time="0.8s" /> If only it were another hat, she thought, for her lace frock and her big hat seemed to shine in the dark, and surely everyone was looking at her.
